context:
Timing method: compare the batch start head (base) with the member head on the locked engine versions (record `polars`, `datafusion`, `pyspark` versions). Run base and member alternately, one warm-up then five timed runs each, and compare the best time per cell. A cell is one query on one platform at one scale factor. Scale factors SF1 and SF10; platforms polars-df, datafusion-df, pyspark-df unless stated otherwise.

Evidence so far: on Polars 1.44.2, `{1, NULL}` gives n_unique 2 and min != max false; `{NULL, NULL}` gives min != max NULL. On pandas 3.0.5, drop_duplicates then size gives 2 for `{1, NULL}`. The lock pins datafusion 54.0.0, polars 1.44.2, pyspark 4.2.0; the earlier measurements used newer engines, so the gate must be measured on the locked versions. On DuckDB 2.0.0 an isolated-step slowdown did not carry to complete queries, which is why complete queries decide.

Timing needs no core change: the harness runs the same complete query from two checkouts (batch start head and member head), so no pattern switch is added to the code. Modin and cuDF share the pandas helpers and are not tested locally; say so in the landing report.
description:
Problem. TPC-DS Q16, Q94 and Q95 keep orders shipped from more than one warehouse (SQL: `EXISTS (... ws1.ws_warehouse_sk <> ws2.ws_warehouse_sk)` on the same order). The DataFrame code in `benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/queries.py` has three ways to compute that:
- `_web_multi_warehouse_orders_expression` (Q94 with `optimized=false` always takes the self-join; Q95 with `optimized=true` takes group-by plus `n_unique()`), and `q16_expression_impl` (group-by plus `n_unique()`).
- Both contain a branch for `platform == "datafusion"`. The DataFusion adapter's `platform_name` is "DataFusion", so the branch never runs.
- The pandas implementations (`_web_multi_warehouse_pandas`, `q16_pandas_impl`) drop duplicate (order, warehouse) pairs and count rows.

Defects. (a) On Polars, `n_unique()` counts NULL, so Q95 treats an order with warehouses {1, NULL} as multi-warehouse; SQL does not. Q16 filters NULL first and is correct. (b) `_web_multi_warehouse_pandas` has the same error for Q94 and Q95 on the pandas family. Neither has produced a wrong published answer: TPC-DS orders have about ten lines, so almost every order has two real warehouses. (c) Dead branches. (d) On isolated-step measurements (DataFusion 55.0.0, Polars 2.1.0, PySpark 4.3.0, shared machine) a min/max comparison was fastest in 39 of 40 tests.

Change. One helper that groups by order number and keeps orders where `min(warehouse_sk) != max(warehouse_sk)`; `min`/`max` skip NULL and an all-NULL order yields NULL, which the filter drops. Use it for Q16, Q94 and Q95 on the expression family; apply the same rule in both pandas implementations. Remove both platform branches, the `optimized_multi_warehouse` parameter, and its arguments for queries 94 and 95 in `helper_query_specs.yaml`.

Decision gate (pattern choice, decided by the timing gate below, by the leader):
- PASS: no cell is more than 10% slower than base -> keep min/max on every platform.
- FAIL: any cell is more than 10% slower -> replace min/max on every platform with a distinct count over rows whose warehouse is not NULL, time again, and record both tables. The NULL fix and the branch removal land in either case. If the fallback is also more than 10% slower than base on any cell, stop and ask the owner.

Frozen scope: `benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/queries.py`, `benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/helper_query_specs.yaml`, `tests/unit/core/tpcds/**`.

Guardrails (all members of batch df-distinct-remediation):
- Stay inside the frozen scope listed below; a path outside it is refused at landing.
- No platform-name branch may select a query pattern. One rule for every platform.
- Do not edit SQL query text, reference answers, expected-result fixtures, or equivalence baselines to make a check pass. A changed answer is a defect in the change.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). No new helper before `make duplicate-check-delta` shows no equivalent.
- Members make no tracker call of any kind, open no PR, and do not run the fast tier. They use absolute paths under their own worktree and stop at a landing report.
- Timing runs only through `make heavy-run CMD='...'` after `make heavy-status`, on an idle machine: 1-minute load average at or below 3.0 before every pass. A pass that starts or ends above that is discarded, not averaged in.
- Timing harness scripts are throwaway and are not committed; results go under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/df-distinct-remediation/ and are summarised in this item's context.
- Do not touch Q28's explicit NULL filter or any other query in `queries.py`.
- Do not change `unified_frame.py`; the shared method belongs to `df-n-unique-null-semantics`. This member's tests must pass with and without that change.
